items.text: Stand in your court robes at the top of the eastern steps to keep the spirits of your departed undisturbed in their shrines when villagers drive away pestilential influences.
items.quote: Confucius would stand at the top of his eastern steps, in his court robes, to keep the spirits (of his departed) undisturbed in their shrines.
items.conflict: Treating the dead as if their spirits reside in shrines and can be disturbed.

items.text: Provide for the sacrifice at the earth altar in the open court of your house, showing gratitude to the source of your prosperity.
items.quote: (The Heads of) families provided (for the sacrifice to it) at the altar in the open court (of their houses)
items.conflict: Offering to the earth as a spirit, not to God.

work: The Single Victim At The Border Sacrifices
heading: Liji 9 · Jiao Te Sheng 郊特牲 · The Single Victim At The Border Sacrifices · Jiao Te Sheng II.14 … Jiao Te Sheng III.7

items.text: Remain faithful to him all her life; when he dies, do not remarry.
items.quote: Once mated with her husband, all her life she will not change (her feeling of duty to him) and hence, when the husband dies she will not marry (again).
items.conflict: Widow remarriage is permitted in 1 Corinthians 7:39; forbidding it goes beyond Scripture.

work: The Single Victim At The Border Sacrifices
heading: Liji 9 · Jiao Te Sheng 郊特牲 · The Single Victim At The Border Sacrifices · Jiao Te Sheng II.2 … Jiao Te Sheng II.13

items.text: Show affection to your father by honouring him in the sacred rites.
items.quote: the tortoise-shell was operated on in that of his father; affection shown to his father

items.text: Honour your great ancestor by seeking his blessing in his fane.
items.quote: received the reply in the fane of his (great) ancestor; honour being thus done to his ancestor

items.text: Venerate your superiors as the king taught the people.
items.quote: showing the people how they ought to venerate their superiors

work: The Single Victim At The Border Sacrifices
heading: Liji 9 · Jiao Te Sheng 郊特牲 · The Single Victim At The Border Sacrifices · Jiao Te Sheng III.22 … Jiao Te Sheng III.29

items.text: Perform the whole sacrifice yourself, yielding nothing to assistants, showing all reverence.
items.quote: the principal himself gave every demonstration of reverence and performed all his admirable service without yielding anything to any one.
items.conflict: Reverence due to God alone; ancestor veneration risks idolatry (Exod 20:3-6).

items.text: Show extreme reverence by bowing twice with head to the ground, baring your breast, and personally applying the knife.
items.quote: the ruler bowed twice with his head to the ground, and, with breast bared, himself applied the knife
items.conflict: Reverence due to God alone; ancestor veneration risks idolatry (Exod 20:3-6).

items.text: Call yourself 'the filial son' or 'filial grandson' and act accordingly, demonstrating filial piety in the sacrifice.
items.quote: When the sacrificer styled himself 'the filial son,' or 'the filial grandson,' he did so (in all cases) according to the meaning of the name.
items.conflict: Ancestor rites can slip into worship of the dead; honor parents while alive (Eph 6:2).

items.text: Purify the water and liquor so they are bright and new, symbolizing sincerity.
items.quote: In the bright water and the clear liquor the thing valued was their newness.
items.conflict: External purification cannot substitute for a clean heart (Matt 15:11).

items.text: Prepare the flesh as prescribed, but know that the spirit's enjoyment is unknowable; show reverence to the utmost.
items.quote: The flesh of the victim might be presented raw and as a whole, or cut up in pieces, or sodden, or thoroughly cooked; but how could they know whether the spirit enjoyed it? The sacrificer simply showed his reverence to the utmost of his power.
items.conflict: The dead do not eat; offerings cannot reach them (Ps 115:17).

items.text: When your descendant serves as personator, bow to him and put him at ease, honoring the spirit he represents.
items.quote: (When the representative of the departed) had made the libation with the kiâ cup, or the horn, (the sacrificer) was told (to bow to him) and put him at ease.
items.conflict: Bowing to a person as spirit-representative can imply worship of the dead; reserve religious honor for God (Rev 22:8-9).

items.text: When you serve as the personator of the departed, stand when inactive and sit when active, as befits the spirit's presence.
items.quote: Anciently, the representative stood when nothing was being done; when anything was being done, he sat. He personated the spirit
items.conflict: Impersonating a dead ancestor is a form of necromancy or spiritual deception (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: During the three days of purification, fix your thoughts on the unseen and the departed, until you seem to see them.
items.quote: Hence after the three days of purification, the superior man was sure (to seem) to see those to whom his sacrifice was to be offered.
items.conflict: Seeking visions of the dead is forbidden (Lev 19:31).

items.text: Offer sacrifices for the purposes of prayer, thanksgiving, or deprecation.
items.quote: Sacrifices were for the purpose of prayer, or of thanksgiving, or of deprecation.
items.conflict: Sacrifices belong to God alone, not to the dead (Heb 9:14).

items.text: Strain and clarify the liquor with white grass and pure liquor, making the offering pure.
items.quote: In straining (the new liquor) for the cup, they used the white (mâo) grass and obtained a clear cup.
items.conflict: Purity of offering does not reach the dead; trust in Christ's once-for-all sacrifice (Heb 10:10).

items.text: Show reverence and affection to your wife, as the ancient kings did, and lead her with wisdom.
items.quote: It was by such reverence and affection for their wives that the ancient kings obtained the kingdom.

items.text: In your youth, follow and obey your father.
items.quote: in her youth, she follows her father and elder brother

items.text: In your youth, follow and obey your elder brother.
items.quote: in her youth, she follows her father and elder brother

items.text: When married, follow and obey your husband.
items.quote: when married, she follows her husband

items.text: When your husband is dead, follow and obey your son.
items.quote: when her husband is dead, she follows her son

items.text: Serve your husband's parents: prepare and present food to them, and eat what they leave as a mark of regard.
items.quote: the wife, having washed her hands, prepared and presented (a sucking-pig) to her husband's parents; and when they had done eating, she ate what was left

items.text: Perform the ancestral sacrifices with utmost care, offering the proper things and seeking the spirit of the departed.
items.quote: They knew not whether the spirit were here, or whether it were there, or far off, away from all men.
items.conflict: No offering for the dead; Christ's once-for-all sacrifice (Heb 10:10)
